aim.en: Find the resistance R of a resistor from readings of potential difference and current.

text.en: Drag each component onto the board. The ammeter goes in series; the voltmeter goes across the resistor.
Move the rheostat slider to change the current.
Read the voltmeter and the ammeter and record V and I. Repeat for 6 settings.
Plot the graph, choose the formula and finish your report.

relation.en: V is directly proportional to I

options.text: R = slope of V against I

text.en: I opened the switch between readings so the resistor did not heat up.
I made sure the connections were tight.
I checked the meters for zero error and read them straight on.
I connected the ammeter across the resistor.
I kept the current as large as possible the whole time.
V is proportional to I at constant temperature, so the resistor obeys Ohm's law.
The current falls as the potential difference rises.
The resistance changes a lot as the current changes.
